title: nightshift-soft-ecc-accumulation-and-cuda-context-loss-annotated-notes
content:
Summary:
Night shift encountered recurring soft ECC errors on a subset of GPU nodes that slowly accumulated over many hours and culminated in CUDA context failures and driver watchdog resets. Behavior was intermittent: corrected ECC count increments followed by sudden nvidia-uvm / CUDA context loss and then an automatic driver reset. This doc collects: timeline, quick triage steps used, hypothesized root causes, short-term mitigations applied during the shift, and proposed telemetry + alert changes.

Top-line impact:
- Affected pool: inference-gpu-pool-west-2 (fleet tag: prod-rt-infer)
- Symptom: jobs failing with "CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION" and later node reboots or nvidia-driver reloads (watchdog).
- Customer visible: 3 customers saw increased error rate for 30–90s windows; traffic rerouted by autoscaler in 2 cases.

Immediate on-call timeline (annotated):
- 2025-09-18 01:12 UTC: Pager alert (gpu.ecc.corrected_rate spike) — oncall picked up (Miguel).
- 01:20 UTC: dcgm-exporter showed sustained corrected ECC increments on GPUs 0,2,3 of node infer-023. Rates ~ 50 corrected/min on one GPU over 10 minutes.
- 01:28 UTC: First job failure observed: framework error -> CUDA context lost -> container crash.
- 01:30 UTC: Attempted live debug: used "nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,HWUtil" and dcgm metrics; kernel logs show repeated "NVRM: Xid" messages.
- 01:33 UTC: Driver watchdog triggered; kernel logged stack trace. Node's kworker threads pegged high.
- 01:40 UTC: Actions: drained node (k8s cordon + evict), triggered remote modprobe/nvidia restart (didn't persist), reboot scheduled.
- 02:05 UTC: After reboot, node came up clean; ECC counters reset; no immediate recurrence but several adjacent nodes showed low corrected ECC upticks.
- Post-incident: compiled notes, opened JIRA-INC-2145, added telemetry gaps.

Log excerpts (paraphrased):
- kernel: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, PID 11245, GPU 0000:3b:00.0"
- dmesg: repeated i2c timeout on GPU 2 prior to ECC ramp (timestamp -20s)
- dcgm: gpu.ecc.corrected_total: +120 over 12 minutes for GPU 2
- nvidia-driver: "NVRM: GPU is being reset due to a hang"

Triage notes & commands used (quick recipe):
1) Capture DCGM and nvidia-smi snapshots immediately:
   - sudo dcgmi discovery -l; sudo dcgmi dmon -e ecc,curr_usage -s 1 -c 30
   - nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,BOARD,GPU,ENCODER,COMPUTE
2) Check kernel/Xid codes and correlate time with job traces:
   - sudo journalctl -k -u kubelet --since "15 minutes ago" | grep -i nvrm
   - grep "NVRM: Xid" /var/log/kern.log
3) Inspect thermal and power rails around timestamp:
   - ipmitool sensor list; smartctl for host drives if relevant
4) Live mitigation if ECC ramping but node still usable:
   - cordon + drain the node in k8s to stop new jobs
   - set node label to avoid re-scheduling: kubectl label node NODE degraded=true --overwrite
5) If driver is hung and modprobe doesn't recover, schedule reboot via SRE playbook

Hypotheses considered (ranked):
- H1: Thermal cycling / fan curve issues causing marginal ECC events that accumulate and disturb GPU memory sections -> leads to occasional illegal instructions. Evidence: i2c timeouts and ambient temp log shows short fan RPM dips.
- H2: NVLink fabric flapping cascades into memory controller errors for peer GPUs (less likely, no NVLink errors seen in dcgm).
- H3: Driver bug in interaction with unified memory under heavy multi-tenant eviction -> corner-case causing stale pointers and illegal instruction (some Xid patterns align with known driver oops).
- H4: Subtle hardware marginality (one DIMM/VRAM bank degrading) causing increased correctable ECC rate prior to an uncorrectable event.

Short-term mitigations applied during the incident:
- Node drained and rebooted (staged reboot to avoid cascade).
- Temporarily widened ECC-rate alert thresholds to reduce noise while we investigate (note: this is a stop-gap and must be reverted).
- Added temporary autoscaler rule to avoid scheduling short-lived GPU batch jobs onto nodes showing >20 corrected/min for >5 minutes.

Observability & telemetry gaps (urgent):
- Missing: per-GPU corrected ECC rate alert with lookback bucketing (we had total counters but not rate windowed).
- Missing: correlation metric between pci bus errors/i2c timeouts and corrected ECC.
- Missing: GPU driver oops (Xid) event ingest into tracing so that a trace can jump to customer request ids.

Concrete proposals (near-term roadmap items):
1) Metrics/Alerting (Priority P0/P1):
   - Add a new time-series: gpu.ecc.corrected_rate (per-gpu, 1m and 10m windows) with a default alert: warn at 20 corrected/min sustained 5m, page at 50 corrected/min sustained 3m.
   - Add event ingestion pipeline for "NVRM: Xid" messages to attach to node-level incident timelines (link to tracing ids).
2) Dashboards:
   - Small heatmap panel showing corrected_rate across the pool for the last 60min to catch migrating hot GPUs.
   - Panel correlating i2c/pci error counts and fan RPM on same time axis.
3) Runbook updates (this doc -> canonical runbook):
   - Add step-by-step for building a per-gpu snapshot (dcgm + nvidia-smi + journalctl) and the quick-modules-and-reboot decision tree.
   - Add field recipe: if corrected_rate > 100/min immediately cordon + drain and open hardware ticket.
4) Hardware validation:
   - For nodes showing repeated ECC drifts, schedule a memtest-like job: heavy read-modify tests across full VRAM to try to reproduce.
   - If repro occurs, escalate to HW vendor.
5) Runtime mitigation experiments (dev team):
   - Test driver upgrade candidate (staging only) with improved handling of certain Xid codes (link PR).
   - Evaluate pinning heavy batch jobs to dedicated subtree to reduce multi-tenant interference.

Post-incident root-cause analysis plan:
- Collect historical dcgm metrics from last 72h for affected node group, plot corrected_rate vs ambient temp and fan RPM.
- Cross-check BIOS/firmware revisions across fleet for pattern.
- Run GPU stress tests targeted at memory banks on suspect GPUs.
- Re-run with driver candidate in staging to reproduce.

Open action items (owners & dates):
- Miguel: attach dcgm 72h plots to JIRA-INC-2145 (due 2025-09-20).
- Aisha: implement gpu.ecc.corrected_rate series and basic alert in dev-monitoring (due 2025-09-22).
- Connor: draft canonical runbook page from this doc and PR to Confluence (due 2025-09-24).
- Priya: coordinate HW repro and vendor contact if repro confirmed (status: pending).

Notes to self / oncall tips:
- "Corrected" ECC surges are important — they often preface worse failures. Don't ignore steady ramps.
- Xid code 79/43 pattern might map to memory access issues; look for adjacent pci/i2c messages.
- Reboots are safer than repeated modprobe attempts if the node is production-serving and contexts are leaking.
- Keep a short-lived tag/annotation on cordoned nodes to avoid accidental unschedule.

Unresolved questions:
- Why did reboot clear the problem briefly? (masking vs real fix?)
- Are particular job types more likely to surface these issues (large unified memory allocations)?
- Any correlation with maintenance windows or power cycling?

Appendix: useful commands collected during triage:
- sudo dcgmi dmon -e ecc,sm,mem -s 1 -c 120  # short live capture
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,index,ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu_ecc.csv
- sudo journalctl -k | grep -i "NVRM: Xid" --no-pager
- kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force

References and links:
- Driver PR to try: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/678
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INC-2145
- Dashboard temp: confluence:gpu-ecc-observability-overview
- Slack incident thread: slack:#sre-incident-2145

End notes: this doc is a working capture from a night-shift triage; needs to be converted to a formal runbook and added to the standard SRE playbooks. Please add any missing command snippets or corrections inline and ping me (Priya) — leaving rough TODOs above.
